01_library: I keep a library of scanned books on a home server. Nine thousand of them.
02_moma: This is one: MoMA's first exhibition catalogue, from nineteen twenty-nine. The museum gives these away as P.D.F.s, seven hundred and fifty-seven of them.
03_problem: A scan is a picture of a page. You can't search it; nobody knows which paintings are inside. With no text layer, it can't even tell you which book it is. A quarter of my library is anonymous.
04_goal: So for this hackathon I built Colophon, to make a scanned library behave like a catalogued one. Two jobs. Find and read every picture on every page, so you can search for what you remember. And identify every book from its own pages, so no scan stays anonymous.
05_sam: How it works. SAM three point one draws a box around every picture on every page: painting, photograph, drawing, print, sculpture, map, diagram. It runs on my own machines, two DGX Sparks and a gaming PC, a page a second each.
06_read: Muse Spark then reads each page with its boxes numbered: what every picture shows, and its caption as printed, artist, title, year, medium. A second call reads a book's title page and copyright page and returns a catalogue record, checked against Open Library before it is trusted.
07_search: Now type what you remember: a woman reading a letter. Seurat's drawing, nineteen twenty-nine, page one twenty-five. A city street at night: Van Gogh's café terrace.

And because the captions were read, a painting can be followed across catalogues. Picasso's Green Still Life, six times between nineteen thirty-one and nineteen thirty-six. Which catalogue reproduced which work: that index did not exist.
08_identifier: And the identifier. Title page and copyright page in, a record out, with the page each field came from. The I.S.B.N. checks out against Open Library: verified.

It could be tested honestly: page one of every MoMA P.D.F. is MoMA's own record. Hidden from the model and used as the answer key for all seven hundred and fifty-seven books: title ninety-four percent, year ninety, publisher eighty-six, author eighty-five, I.S.B.N. ninety-two.
It even found MoMA's mistakes: this brochure says nineteen eighty-seven on the sheet; the pages say two thousand and five.
09_scale: In two days all seven hundred and fifty-seven catalogues went through: seventy-seven thousand pages, ninety-three thousand pictures found, the oldest fifty-three catalogues read and searchable. The rest is a matter of running it, at half a cent a page. The code and every number are on GitHub. Next: my own nine thousand books.
10_close: Colophon. A library that knows what is on its pages.
